title: Sparkling Water 12-pack

drivers.name: Promotion: 20% off
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted uplift from 10 past 20%+ promotions: x1.58 vs baseline. Deeper than 2026-07-20 (x1.55), but consistent with history.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery warning
drivers.evidence: Planner notes indicate risk of short delivery, reducing supply availability. No past event to calibrate, so moderate downside shrink.

drivers.name: Halloween (week before)
drivers.evidence: Historical x0.68 vs baseline (2 occurrences). This week is 2 weeks after Halloween, so no direct effect, but residual impact on demand may linger. Not applicable.

adjustment.analysis: The 20% off promotion is deeper than previous 20% discounts (e.g., 2026-06-29, 2026-07-20), but the 25% off in 2026-07-20 drove x1.55 vs baseline, and the noise-adjusted uplift is x1.58. The classical model’s +58% is consistent. However, the prior week (2026-09-28) sold 110 vs baseline 95.5 (x1.15), and recent weeks show no trend. The store is not in a holiday rush; Halloween is next week (week before), which historically lowers demand by x0.68. This week’s promotion is not a holiday, so no offset. Supplier warning adds downside risk. Shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence on supply impact. Use noise-adjusted uplift for promotion. No trend in recent weeks, so baseline is stable.

brief:
PRODUCT: Sparkling Water 12-pack | category Beverages | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25 (2 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Promotion: 20% off
  shelf price: 4.94 (-19.9% vs regular price 6.17)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 95.5 | 5%-95%: 28.9 - 183.3 | 10%-90%: 61.2 - 151.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-39% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
